explanations.explanation: Birds, friend. Jesus says some seed fell along the path, and “…the birds came and devoured it.” The seed was out in the open on that path, and the birds took it. Sown and swallowed in one verse is the fastest turnaround I've ever seen from a seed.

Locusts are a good guess for a field story, but they don't show up here. Jesus says it was the birds that came and devoured the seed along the path. So keep the locusts out of this one, because this parable has no room for them.
Foxes have a sneaky reputation, so I see the pick. But the text says the birds came and devoured the seed on the path. There isn't a single fox in the verse, friend.

I see the logic, but Jesus says it the other way around: “It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.” So the seed comes up quick, not slow. Shallow soil, fast sprout. I think that fast start is worth keeping in your pocket for what happens next.

That's right, it's false. The text says, “It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.” Quick, not slow. That seed was in a hurry, and I think a hurried start is worth remembering as the story goes on.

No root, that's the reason. Jesus says, “But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.” The seed sprang up quickly, but nothing was holding it below. I know the feeling of looking sharp and being shaky underneath, friend.

Wind doesn't appear in this verse. Jesus says the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root. The sun did the scorching, and the missing root is the reason the text gives.
There's no rain in this one, friend. It's the sun that rises and scorches the seedlings, and Jesus says they withered because they had no root. If anything, the trouble here was heat, not water.
Choke is the word. The thorns “…grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.” That is a rough neighborhood for a seedling. It never even gets to produce a crop.
Shade sounds friendly, I'll give you that. But the verse says the thorns grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop. That is not a cozy spot to be planted.
Protect would be nice, but the thorns do the opposite. Jesus says they grew up and choked the seedlings, and the seedlings yielded no crop. Those thorns were not looking out for anybody.

True, and it's a relief after three rough landings. On the good soil the seed “…sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop…” Three steps, and this seed makes every one of them. Finally some good news in the field.
It's actually true, friend. Jesus says the seed on good soil “…sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop…” After all the bad news, this soil comes through. It sprouts, it grows, and it produces.

Yes, they asked Him about the parable. Verse 10 says that as soon as Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, they asked Him about it. They had a question and they asked it, which is always the smart move.

The crowd was part of the scene in verse 1, but the question isn't about them. Verse 10 says the Twelve and those around Him asked about the parable. The people on the shore are the setting, not the topic.

The boat is where Jesus sat in verse 1, but verse 10 says they asked Him about the parable. When Jesus is alone with the Twelve and those around Him, the parable is the topic. A boat makes a fine seat, but it's not the question the text gives.

explanations.answer: The mystery of the kingdom of God
explanations.explanation: Verse 11: “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you…” That's what Jesus says to the Twelve and those around Him. Then comes the other side, that to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables. I know what it's like to be handed something I never expected, like a whole bakery after years in a junk drawer.

explanations.answer: The keys of the kingdom of heaven
explanations.explanation: Keys of the kingdom of heaven is a real phrase, but Jesus uses it in a different scene (Matthew 16:19). Here He says what has been given to this group is “The mystery of the kingdom of God…” Close neighborhood, different verse.

Authority over unclean spirits is something Jesus gives the Twelve later in Mark (Mark 6:7). In this verse, what has been given is “The mystery of the kingdom of God…” That's a different gift from a different scene, friend.

explanations.answer: They might turn and be forgiven
explanations.explanation: That's the line: “otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.” It comes right after the words about ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding. I'll be honest, friend, this is one of the weightier verses in the chapter. I'd read it slowly.

explanations.answer: They might go and tell others
explanations.explanation: Telling others isn't in the words Jesus quotes. The line says “otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.” Turning and being forgiven is what it names, so that's the one to hold onto.
Becoming teachers doesn't appear in those words either. What the quote names is that they might “…turn and be forgiven.” Keep it to what the words say, friend, and the words say turn and be forgiven.

explanations.answer: Satan comes and takes it away
explanations.explanation: Satan comes and takes the word away. Jesus says, “As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.” Notice the words “As soon as…” That is quick work.

explanations.answer: They argue it out of their heads
explanations.explanation: Nobody argues in this verse. Jesus says that as soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them. It's Satan doing the taking, not a debate.

Forgetting by morning is a very human guess, and I've forgotten plenty before breakfast. But Jesus says Satan comes “As soon as they hear it…” and takes away the word. So the verse names who does the taking.

explanations.answer: Trouble or persecution over the word
explanations.explanation: Trouble or persecution because of the word, that's what does it. Jesus says, “When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.” They received it with joy, but they have no root. Joy at the start, no root underneath.

explanations.answer: Growing bored of the same message
explanations.explanation: Boredom isn't named anywhere in these verses. Jesus says what makes them fall away is trouble or persecution that comes because of the word. They received it with joy, so the text shows an excited start, not a dull one.

explanations.answer: Finding a new teacher they prefer
explanations.explanation: Another teacher isn't in the verse. Jesus says they fall away when trouble or persecution comes because of the word. Nobody is shopping around here, friend. It's the trouble that does it.
It's actually false, friend. Jesus says “…they quickly fall away.” Quickly, not slowly over many years. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, there's no long goodbye.

False is right. The verse says that when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, “…they quickly fall away.” That's fast, not many years. It also says they remain for only a season, which fits.

True. Jesus says the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, “…and it becomes unfruitful.” That matches the thorn seedlings in verse 7, which yielded no crop. Same ending, now with the meaning spelled out.

It's actually true, friend. Jesus says the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, “…and it becomes unfruitful.” Unfruitful is the word He uses. That's the same result as the seedlings that yielded no crop.

explanations.answer: Receive it and produce a crop
explanations.explanation: They hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop. Jesus says so in verse 20, with a crop of thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold. The rocky-ground people received it too, but these ones go on to produce a crop.

Studying and teaching others isn't what verse 20 says. It says they “…hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop…” I'd happily study alongside you, friend, but those three are the ones Jesus names.

explanations.answer: Keep it and tell no one
explanations.explanation: Keeping it and telling no one isn't in the verse. The good-soil people hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop. A crop, to my eye, is not something you can hide in your pocket.
A stand, that's the answer. Jesus asks, “Doesn’t he set it on a stand?” Nobody lights a lamp and then tucks it under a basket or a bed. A lamp belongs up where it can do its job.
Floor sounds reasonable, but Jesus says a stand. He asks, “Doesn’t he set it on a stand?” A stand lifts the lamp up, while a floor would just have you tripping over it.

Doorstep is a good guess for someone who wants visitors, I'll admit. But Jesus says the lamp goes on a stand, as in “Doesn’t he set it on a stand?” The basket and the bed are the places nobody puts it.

It's actually false, friend. Jesus says, “…there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.” By that verse, nothing concealed stays hidden forever. I know a good secret is tempting, but that's what He says.

False is right. Jesus says, “For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.” He says it right after the lamp. So nothing concealed stays hidden forever.

explanations.answer: Even more will be added to you
explanations.explanation: Even more will be added to you. Jesus says, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.” It's a generous verse, friend, and it starts with paying attention.

explanations.answer: Nothing more will be added to you
explanations.explanation: Nothing more is the opposite of what Jesus says. After the measure line, He says “…and even more will be added to you.” Even more, not nothing more. It's a generous line.

explanations.answer: Less will be given back to you
explanations.explanation: Less given back would make it sound like a bad deal, but that's not what Jesus says. He says “…it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.” Even more, friend.

explanations.answer: Even what he has will be taken away
explanations.explanation: Verse 25 says, “For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” That's a hard line. I think it's the kind of saying that makes you slow down and read it again, so go ahead.

explanations.answer: He will be given a little to start
explanations.explanation: A little to start sounds kind, but it's not in the verse. Jesus says whoever does not have, “…even what he has will be taken away from him.” It's a hard line, and I think it's worth reading slowly.

explanations.answer: He will be given exactly what he needs
explanations.explanation: Exactly what he needs isn't in the verse either. Jesus says whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have, “…even what he has will be taken away from him.” Sticking to His words is the safest way to read this one.
Not quite, it's false. Jesus says the man sleeps and wakes night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, “…though he knows not how.” He doesn't know how it happens. The seed does it anyway.
False is right. The verse says the seed sprouts and grows “…though he knows not how.” The man sleeps and wakes, and the seed keeps going. I bet that man sleeps better than I do.
True. Jesus says, “All by itself the earth produces a crop…” In this parable the man scatters the seed, and the earth does the producing. Stalk, head, grain, all by itself.
It's actually true, friend. Verse 28 says, “All by itself the earth produces a crop…” The man scatters the seed, and the earth does the producing.
Stalk, then head, then grain. Jesus says, “…first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.” There's no skipping ahead in that line. Everything in its turn.
That flips the first two. Jesus says, “…first the stalk, then the head…” The stalk comes first, then the head, then the grain.
Grain comes last, not first. Jesus says, “…first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.” Grain is the finish line of that list, friend.
Sickle. Jesus says, “…he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.” As soon as the grain is ripe, the man gets to work. Good timing from a good farmer.

A hammer is handy, but it's not the tool in this verse. The man swings the sickle as soon as the grain is ripe, because the harvest has come. Swinging a hammer at a field would look funny, I'll say that much.
A staff is a fine walking stick, but Jesus names a sickle. The man swings it as soon as the grain is ripe, because the harvest has come. Nobody's harvesting grain with a walking stick, friend.
True. Jesus says the mustard seed “…is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.” That is one tiny seed. Keep that in mind for the very next verse.
It's actually true, friend. Jesus says it's “…the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.” That's how He describes it. Small is the word.

explanations.answer: The largest of all garden plants
explanations.explanation: The largest of all garden plants. Jesus says, “…it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches…” From the smallest seed to the largest plant, friend. That is some glow-up.

explanations.answer: A small bush in the corner
explanations.explanation: A small bush in the corner is far too modest. Jesus says it grows to be the largest of all garden plants. Smallest seed, largest plant.

A vine along the ground stays low, but Jesus says it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches. Great branches is a long way from creeping along the ground. Nothing low-key about this plant.

It's actually false, and it comes down to one animal word. Jesus says it puts forth great branches “…so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.” Birds, not cattle. Great branches, and birds nesting in the shade.
False is right. Jesus says it puts forth great branches “…so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.” Birds, not cattle of the field. Those cows would have to look elsewhere for shade.

He explains everything to them. Verse 34 says He did not tell the crowd anything without a parable, “But privately He explained everything to His own disciples.” Private lessons, friend. I'd have signed up.

explanations.answer: He tells them even more parables
explanations.explanation: More parables is a fair guess, since this chapter is full of them. But the verse says privately He explained everything to His own disciples. Explaining is what He does privately with His own disciples.

explanations.answer: He asks them to explain to Him
explanations.explanation: Jesus asking them to explain it to Him would be backwards. Verse 34 says privately He explained everything to His own disciples. He's the one doing the explaining, friend.
